Rows That Have No Partner in a Join

Source: R/derive.R
sv_unmatched.Rd

Returns the rows of one table that a join check counts as unmatched, so the number on the join step can be opened as a table. With no rule the keys are compared as dplyr::anti_join() compares them (NA matches NA), and the rows are anti_join(x, y, by). With a date rule a missing key matches nothing (na_matches = "never"); what = "unmatched" gives the rows whose key has no partner at all, and what = "outside_window" the rows that have a key partner but no pair the rule keeps. The two together are the rows the join check counts as unmatched under the rule.

Usage

sv_unmatched(
  x,
  y,
  by,
  rule = NULL,
  side = c("x", "y"),
  what = c("unmatched", "outside_window")
)

Arguments

x, y

Tables: data frames, or duckdb or Arrow tables (these stay lazy).

by

Join columns, as in sv_join_diagnostics().

rule

Optional date rule, as in sv_join_diagnostics().

side

"x" for the rows of x, "y" for the rows of y.

what

"unmatched" or "outside_window" (needs a rule).

Value

The rows of the chosen table, with its columns and row order.

Details

The canvas builds the same rows from its join-check button, and generates code that rebuilds them.

Examples

ae <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("a", "b", NA, "z"), aeterm = c("x", "y", "z", "w"))
dm <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("a", "b", "c"))
sv_unmatched(ae, dm, "USUBJID")
#>   USUBJID aeterm
#> 1    <NA>      z
#> 2       z      w
